problems: The blind guess (sailing boat with curved hull, mast, rigging, on waves) matches the intended ferry well. The wavy water lines under the hull at about y=385 support it.
The figure is the right way up: masthead (282,210) is at the top, the hull is at the bottom, and the pennant (401,232) flies right from the yard end.

Star placement is mostly right. Bow tip 35904 sits at the bottom-left of the hull (244,349). Stern lamp 33579 sits at the bottom-right (374,343). Masthead 35210 is at the top of the sail. Top-right sail corner 33977 is on the yard. Belly lantern 34444 sits in the sail. Pennant 33152 is at the yard end.
Mast foot 35037 at about (294,279) is close to the belly star, so the two read as one cluster. Deck star 35205 at (282,316) sits on the deck line, which is acceptable.

The gold lines form a polygon copy of the outline, and the faint blue silhouette underneath is what gives the hull its curve. The silhouette is real but weak, so the gold lines dominate and the image reads more as a gold polygon than a ship outline.

The sail is a thin quadrilateral rather than a sail shape with a billowing belly, so it reads a bit like a kite or a flag. The hull curve is shallow and could also read as a bowl, which is the second alternative guess.

Labels collide badly. 'deck where the bow meets the gunwale' overlaps 'gunwale amidships'. 'bow tip of the hull' runs into the gunwale label. 'belly of the sail, the lantern' overlaps 'foot of the mast'. 'pennant' runs off the right edge of the frame's natural area. This makes the labelled image hard to verify, though it does not change the drawing itself.
output.advice: Keep the figure. Optional tweaks if you redraw later: (1) Strengthen the blue hull and sail silhouette so it reads as a real outline, not just the gold polygon. Trace the hull from bow 35904 (244,349) through the bottom curve near (300,378) up to stern lamp 33579 (374,343), then the gunwale rising through 33856 (~358,318) and 35205 (282,316). (2) Make the sail a fuller curve from masthead 35210 (282,210) to 33977 (354,222) down to belly 34444 (325,281), not a straight-edged quadrilateral, so it is less kite-like. (3) Move the labels for 35037, 34444, 35205 and 33856 to separate leader lines so they stop overlapping.
